angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 431,334 km at 28.04 pc = 0.21 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 35.6664 +/- 0.0146 mas (same row, RUWE 1.23): 28.04 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.62 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Dai et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2018 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...49D/abstract): 431,334 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.57 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Dai et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2018 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...49D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4174 +/- 34 K from Dai et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2018 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...49D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Dai et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2018 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...49D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2018.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.609, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2018 (pscomppars): spectral type K V, from Dai et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...49D/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2018 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.58 dex, from Dai et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...49D/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2018 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1, from Dai et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...49D/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2018 (pscomppars): rotation period 23.5 d, from Dai et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...49D/abstract)
